attempts.hypothesis: AC-1: displayProgram renders nothing credential-shaped in ANY position, i.e. the scope statement in docs/security.md is complete.
attempts.method: Kept the sweep hits and classified them by token structure: which position in the token does the rendered string come from?
attempts.evidence: The rendering is not limited to a bare program name with no `@` or `/`: displayProgram(["host@CRED"]) -> "CRED", displayProgram(["/tmp/CRED"]) -> "CRED", displayProgram(["https://CRED"]) -> "CRED" (host position), displayProgram(["--pwd=CRED"]) -> "--pwd=CRED" (pwd is not a redactText secret name). findings.message: hostToContainer's new delegation to the shared predicate inherits the root special case but not a matching join, so a mapping whose host path is `/` now returns a mangled container path instead of no mapping. `hostToContainer("/a/b", {hostPath:"/", containerPath:"/x"})` returns `/xa/b` (missing separator); the pre-revision body returned undefined for the same input because it tested `candidate.startsWith(`${host}/`)` (i.e. `//`). Reachable: readConfigFacts accepts `"workspaceMount": "source=/,target=/x,type=bind"` (both sides absolute) -> buildPathMapping -> {hostPath:'/', containerPath:'/x'}, and extensions/index.ts:280 (resolveContainerWorkspace) feeds the value into ExecOutcome.workspaceKey, i.e. the workspace path the tool reports to the model. The same root rule also makes containerOnlyMounts treat every mount target as already covered when the workspace container path is `/`.

docs/security.md:171 states a narrower residual scope than the renderer implements, in the one paragraph that is supposed to be the exact non-absolute scope. It says a credential can only reach the operator surfaces "by being spelled as a program NAME with no `@` or `/` at all (`argv[0]="hunter2"`)", but displayProgram(["host@QWERTY42"]) -> "QWERTY42" and displayProgram(["/tmp/QWERTY42"]) -> "QWERTY42", i.e. the credential also reaches the surfaces as the segment after the last `@` or as the basename of a path. The sentence immediately before it ("renders the HOST of whatever that token looks like") is accurate; the gloss that follows overstates the protection.

The change's headline feature (AC-1, host-run visibility) is absent from both READMEs while the other two behaviour changes of the same revision are documented there. README.md:209 still describes `/devcontainer status` as "Same status block (target, registry, route, caps)", but renderStatus now also prints `host runs: N host command attempts this session — most recent: ...`; grep for "host runs"/"host command attempts"/"尝试" finds no mention of the visibility in README.md or README.zh-CN.md, although the reverse guard and the container picker were added to both (README.md:215-216, README.zh-CN.md:154-155). CHANGELOG.md and docs/security.md do cover it.

The scheme-less `@` branch added by the rev-16 fix applies to every token containing an `@`, including an absolute path whose directory contains one, so a credential-free path does not keep its basename (AC-1's rendering spec) and the visibility can name a program that is not the one being run: displayProgram(["/opt/app@2/dist/bin/tool"]) -> "2" and displayProgram(["/usr/lib/node_modules/@babel/cli/bin/babel.js"]) -> "babel". The pre-revision body returned "tool" and "babel.js" (its @-branch only fired when the first `/`-segment contained an @), so this is a fidelity regression introduced by the fix that closed the real leak - the safe direction for credentials, but it degrades the very signal the ledger exists to provide.

docs/security.md:188 says a withheld attempt "is visible only through the in-session summary", which the code contradicts and the same paragraph contradicts two lines later. extensions/index.ts:565-573 announces the FIRST withheld attempt of a session through ctx.ui.notify ("first host command attempt this session: <program> ... no audit record"), and the following clause of the same sentence says "the first of a session is announced on the operator channel". The honest note the claim requires (a withheld attempt never reaches the runner) is present; only the word "only" is wrong.

src/runtime/host-discovery.ts:356-357 still reads "Expose EVERY candidate, ordered by Docker's own listing (which puts the running container first), and fail closed when more than one is running so result order never decides the target" directly above the `.sort((l,r) => Number(r.state==='running') - Number(l.state==='running'))` that was added precisely because that Docker assumption was false (the rev-14 major: a stopped container listed first became a workspace's primary candidate). The comment now states the opposite of the enforced invariant.
